title.zh: 直接各向异性参数反演

summary: Connect a real anisotropic forward solve, unit-explicit diagnostics and bounded optimization into a single entry point that consistently preserves a fixed observation size and a valid terminal point.

identity.relation: parameterized forward equilibrium and observations to an anisotropic fit validated at the actual terminal point
identity.direction: initial_params, bounds, observations, solver_config, forward/diagnostic ports and controls -> fit result and separated state
identity.definition: First freeze N from the standard observations, then compose the trial, strict residuals and bounded optimizer. The forward solver_config is deep-copied and params is added; nonconvergence short-circuits first, and failed trials do not participate in the valid best. Optional LHS and the total budget are executed uniformly in the optimizer, and the final parameters, residuals and state are bound to the same fresh evaluation. The current validation includes an analytic manufactured nonzero Green feedback and an independent Biot-Savart/tensor-divergence curved-field recovery.
identity.model: direct inversion composition with caller-specified physical closure, reusing the qualified forward relation and not inventing another anisotropic equilibrium equation
identity.geometry: defined by the forward port; the validated case is an axisymmetric purely poloidal R-Z equilibrium
identity.coordinates: grid [Z,R]; observation positions [R,Z]; optimization vector in fit_keys or bounds order
identity.boundary: The forward port remains responsible for the physical state, pressure closure, boundary and convergence; the graph is responsible for unit-compatible observation connections, the fixed residual protocol and valid parameter control.
assumptions: The physical contracts of equilibrium_solver and diagnostic_evaluator are compatible with the observations.
When binding the current Picard, explicitly state the psi unit Wb/rad, then convert to Wb under the flux observation convention; arbitrary psi is not converted by default.
The penalty is not a physical solution; optimizer stop, forward fixed point, residual fit and identifiability are judged separately.

inputs.name: initial_params
inputs.description: Complete initial values; non-fitted parameters are deep-copied unchanged.
inputs.constraints: All fitted values are finite and lie inside their corresponding bounds.

inputs.name: bounds
inputs.description: Parameter lower and upper bounds and their default order.
inputs.constraints: Every supplied interval is finite with low<high.

inputs.name: method
inputs.constraints: Only least_squares or minimize; the latter explicitly uses L-BFGS-B.

inputs.name: observations
inputs.description: Standard flux_loops and/or thomson multi-channel observations, validated and used to determine N before optimization.
inputs.constraints: values must be nonempty and finite, with positive sigma; every requested channel must be retained. Synthetic diagnostics include points, quantity/unit and profile units.

inputs.name: solver_config
inputs.units: R/Z in m; psi in Wb/rad, B in T, g_psi in Wb/rad/A (current Picard binding)
inputs.constraints: Must satisfy the actual forward contract; no external project environment is required or implied.

inputs.name: equilibrium_solver
inputs.constraints: Must return a boolean converged; if it is not converged and no reason is supplied, add a generic reason; diagnostics are not executed after failure.

inputs.name: diagnostic_evaluator
inputs.description: Diagnostic port for a converged equilibrium.
inputs.constraints: Cannot omit a requested channel; an explicit unit must be accompanied by matching prediction units; no Thomson instrument is assumed inside the graph.

inputs.name: fit_keys
inputs.constraints: Nonempty and duplicate-free, and present in both initial_params and bounds; defaults to the bounds keys.

inputs.name: n_initial_samples
inputs.description: Number of LHS samples before optimization.
inputs.constraints: From 1 to max_evaluations-3; booleans and non-integers are rejected; None does not call LHS.

inputs.name: seed
inputs.dtype: seed accepted by the sampler, or None
inputs.constraints: Ignored when LHS is disabled; the same validated sampler and seed produce the same design.

inputs.name: failure_penalty
inputs.description: Per-component penalty supplied to the optimizer for an invalid trial.
inputs.constraints: Finite and positive, with N*penalty^2 finite; default 1e12.

inputs.name: max_evaluations
inputs.description: Common upper bound on all actual scientific trial calls.
inputs.constraints: At least 3; includes LHS, differences and fresh terminal validation; it must not be confused with SciPy nfev.

outputs.name: best_parameters
outputs.description: The actual revalidated optimizer terminal point; on failure it may be a revalidated historical valid candidate.
outputs.constraints: None if there is no valid candidate. A normal terminal point agrees with optimizer_summary.parameters; no claim is made that it is always the minimum over the whole log.

outputs.name: chi2
outputs.description: Normalized squared sum of the returned state; N*penalty^2 when there is no valid solution.
outputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative; a failure penalty must be read together with the state.

outputs.name: residual_vector
outputs.description: Fixed-size residuals of the same trial that produced the returned state.
outputs.constraints: Parameters, state and residuals belong to the last validated trial; the penalty is returned when there is no valid solution.

outputs.name: converged
outputs.description: The optimizer succeeded and the latest forward evaluation at its actual terminal point is valid.
outputs.constraints: False on fallback, exhausted budget or an invalid terminal point; it does not mean small residuals, a global optimum or identifiability.

outputs.name: forward_converged
outputs.description: The currently returned state has actually passed forward and trial validation.
outputs.constraints: May be True while the optimizer has not converged, indicating a usable partial result.

outputs.name: optimizer_converged
outputs.description: Raw boolean projection of SciPy success.
outputs.constraints: A constant failure penalty can also stop the optimizer; it cannot be treated alone as physical success.

outputs.name: equilibrium
outputs.description: Forward state validated in the same call as best_parameters and residual_vector.
outputs.constraints: None when there is no valid returned candidate.

outputs.name: evaluation_log
outputs.description: Parameters, chi2, valid, failure_reason and source of every actual evaluation.
outputs.constraints: source is latin_hypercube, optimizer, terminal or best_valid_recheck.

outputs.name: failure_reason
outputs.description: Reason for budget exhaustion, numerical failure, terminal failure or optimizer stop.
outputs.constraints: None only when both succeed; contract errors are raised.

outputs.name: optimizer_summary
outputs.description: Method, success, status, message, nfev and parameters from the actual result.x.
outputs.constraints: SciPy nfev is not the total number of scientific calls; it may be None when the budget is interrupted.

outputs.name: best_valid_trial
outputs.description: Complete record of the valid historical trial with the lowest chi2.
outputs.constraints: An observation record only; it is separate from the returned terminal point and must not be assigned another point's convergence state.

outputs.name: scientific_evaluations
outputs.description: Total number of actual trial calls.
outputs.constraints: Does not exceed max_evaluations; includes numerical differences and terminal validation.

outputs.name: max_evaluations
outputs.description: The validated upper bound on scientific calls for this run.

outputs.name: valid_trial_count
outputs.description: Number of valid trials in the evaluation log.

outputs.name: residual_size
outputs.description: Fixed residual size for this run.
outputs.constraints: All vectors have the same size.

outputs.name: identifiability
outputs.constraints: Fixed to not_established; a local stop is not an identifiability proof.

preconditions: Declare a compatible forward relation, pressure closure, observation positions/units, parameter bounds and a fixed budget.
supported: Composition of real anisotropic Picard -> unit-explicit point diagnostics -> fixed-size residuals -> bounded optimization.
A two-parameter analytic manufactured case with nonzero Green feedback, and a curved-field case using an independent discrete tensor/real loop Green.
excluded: Complete reconstruction of an arbitrary experimental device, unknown closure selection, instrument calibration or automatic parameter identifiability.
Using a zero Green or a single-lambda output as the physical qualification of this composition.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Rejects invalid observation layouts, ports, methods, bounds or budgets first; scientific contract errors propagate, and wrong initial values are not retried.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Numerical exceptions are represented by the trial state; optimization budget and runtime failures are reported separately by the optimizer.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: converged requires both optimizer success and a valid fresh terminal evaluation; optimizer_converged and forward_converged are reported separately.
failure_semantics.partial_results: May return a freshly validated partial valid candidate and log without treating it as a completed fit; on complete failure returns a None candidate.

example.description: A real anisotropic Picard recovers the radial pressure gradient and anisotropy ratio on an explicit rank-one nonzero Green manufactured model; observations come from independent analytic formulas. This Green is a test response, not a calibration of a specific device.
example.code:
"""Physical demonstration: two-parameter anisotropic equilibrium recovery driven by independent analytic observations.

The test model uses an explicitly manufactured nonzero rank-one Green response that produces a uniform axial magnetic field.
It verifies the connection among force balance, Green feedback, flux units and inference, and does not impersonate a specific coil device.
No external source code, network access or captured answer is required; observations are generated from independent analytic equations.
"""
import json
import numpy as np
from scirel.equilibrium import solve_axisymmetric_anisotropic_picard
from scirel.diagnostics import synthesize_equilibrium_diagnostics
from scirel.inference import solve_direct_anisotropic_inversion


def case(n=7, true_gradient=1.7, true_ratio=1.6, with_failed_trials=True):
    R,Z=np.meshgrid(np.linspace(.2,.6,n),np.linspace(-.2,.2,n))
    B0,gain=1.,.6
    # Trapezoidal integration is exact for Jphi=a*R/B: C=integral R dR dZ.
    C=(.6**2-.2**2)/2*.4
    B=(B0+np.sqrt(B0**2+4*gain*true_gradient*C))/2
    points=np.array([[R[2,2],Z[2,2]],[R[-2,-2],Z[-2,-2]]])
    psi=B*points[:,0]**2/2
    pperp=5+true_gradient*points[:,0]**2/2
    observations={'flux_loops':{'points':points,'quantity':'magnetic_flux','unit':'Wb',
        'values':2*np.pi*psi,'sigma':1.e-3},
        'thomson':{'points':points,'p_parallel':{'values':true_ratio*pperp,'sigma':.02,'unit':'Pa'},
                   'p_perp':{'values':pperp,'sigma':.02,'unit':'Pa'}}}
    config={'r_grid':R,'z_grid':Z,'psi_vac':B0*R**2/2,
        'g_psi':gain*(R**2/2).ravel()[:,None]*np.ones((1,R.size)),
        'tol':1.e-12,'maxiter':150,'relax':.2}
    calls=[]
    def forward(payload):
        params=payload['params'];a,ratio=params['gradient'],params['ratio']
        p=5+a*R**2/2
        kwargs={k:v for k,v in payload.items() if k!='params'}
        if with_failed_trials and a>2.5:
            kwargs['maxiter']=1  # Deliberately insufficient iteration budget, not a physical bound.
        state=solve_axisymmetric_anisotropic_picard(**kwargs,
            pressure_closure=lambda _b,_psi:{'p_parallel':ratio*p,'p_perpendicular':p})
        calls.append({'gradient':a,'ratio':ratio,'converged':state['converged'],
                      'fixed_point_residual':state['fixed_point_residual'],'iterations':state['iterations']})
        return {**state,'psi_unit':'Wb/rad',
            'profiles':{'p_parallel':state['p_parallel'],'p_perp':state['p_perpendicular']},
            'profile_units':{'p_parallel':'Pa','p_perp':'Pa'}}
    result=solve_direct_anisotropic_inversion(initial_params={'gradient':1.,'ratio':1.2},
        bounds={'gradient':(.2,3.),'ratio':(1.1,2.5)},method='least_squares',
        n_initial_samples=8,seed=3,max_evaluations=140,
        observations=observations,solver_config=config,
        equilibrium_solver=forward,diagnostic_evaluator=synthesize_equilibrium_diagnostics)
    expected={'gradient':true_gradient,'ratio':true_ratio,'B':B,'psi':B*R**2/2,
              'J_phi':true_gradient*R/B,'C':C}
    return result,expected,config,calls


def run():
    result,expected,config,calls=case()
    assert result['converged'] and result['forward_converged']
    for key in ('gradient','ratio'):
        np.testing.assert_allclose(result['best_parameters'][key],expected[key],rtol=1.e-6,atol=0.)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(result['equilibrium']['psi'],expected['psi'],rtol=1.e-10,atol=1.e-12)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(result['equilibrium']['J_phi'],expected['J_phi'],rtol=1.e-10,atol=1.e-12)
    assert result['residual_vector'].shape==(6,)
    assert result['chi2']<1.e-12
    assert any(not x['converged'] for x in calls)
    assert result['best_valid_trial']['valid']
    assert np.max(np.abs(result['equilibrium']['psi']-config['psi_vac']))>1.e-3
    return {'recovered':result['best_parameters'],'truth':{k:expected[k] for k in ('gradient','ratio','B')},
            'chi2':result['chi2'],'residual_count':result['residual_size'],
            'forward_fixed_point_residual':result['equilibrium']['fixed_point_residual'],
            'scientific_evaluations':result['scientific_evaluations'],
            'failed_trials':sum(not x['converged'] for x in calls),
            'maximum_plasma_flux_increment':float(np.max(abs(result['equilibrium']['psi']-config['psi_vac']))),
            'identifiability':'two-parameter manufactured case only; no general inference guarantee',
            'green_model':'declared rank-one uniform-field response; not a calibrated device'}

if __name__=='__main__':
    print(json.dumps(run(),indent=2,ensure_ascii=False))

example_result = run()
assert example_result['residual_count'] == 6
example.expected: Recovers gradient≈1.7 Pa/m^2 and ratio≈1.6; 6 residuals, nonzero flux feedback, actual failed trials and a valid best state. The corresponding result and call budget come from the actual execution record and do not claim applicability to arbitrary devices.

scope: Analytic manufactured two-parameter recovery with 6 residuals; an actually iteration-limited failed trial must not become best.

9-observation independent Biot-Savart loop integral, independent cylindrical tensor divergence and discrete root solution, recovering gradient=4800 and anisotropy=1100, with the anisotropy actually changing the current.
Selected installed-package user calls without a source checkout or development checkout, offline, in a plain virtual environment.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Author regressions, independent analytic and independent discrete-reference comparisons, and selected installed-wheel user calls completed in the exact environment; they cover only the listed contract and examples. Root-level independent intake, human scientific recognition, redistribution permission and public release are separate decisions; they do not extend this to arbitrary closures, devices or global identifiability proofs.
known_limitations: The independent curved-field reference validates the discrete equations on the current finite grid, not a continuum-limit error proof; the same-point zero self-action convention for Green is retained rather than a finite-wire self-field.
The manufactured model is identifiable only within the listed parameter range; the general output remains not_established.
An optimizer stop does not mean the experimental residual threshold is met; the user must judge it against observation noise and the problem itself.
Licensing and human scientific recognition remain independently pending.

nodes.description: Validate the standard observations before any scientific call and freeze N as the total element count of all values.
Validate the actual forward port; only annotate a nonconverged state that lacks a reason.
Validate the actual diagnostic port and retain responsibility for unit matching.
Bind a normalized residual operator with a fixed layout that never drops a channel.
Bind observations, fixed N, fixed configuration and ports; execute per trial through the optimizer and short-circuit diagnostics on nonconvergence.
Bind the existing LHS when a sample count is enabled; the optimizer validates the complete design first.
Validate finite bounds and budget, rank only valid trials; re-evaluate the actual terminal point and separate stop from physical state.
Preserve the complete separated state and only annotate failure results that lack a reason.

execution.ordering: First fix the observation layout and validate the ports, then bind the reducer/trial; optionally bind LHS; the optimizer validates controls and the complete sample design before executing trials and fresh terminal validation, and then returns the state.
branches: When LHS is not enabled, no sampler is bound.
LHS uses only valid candidates as starting points; when no valid LHS candidate exists, the validated initial values are used.
Forward nonconvergence short-circuits diagnostics; a numerical-failure penalty preserves N; contract errors propagate.
When the optimizer's actual terminal point is invalid, only a freshly validated historical valid candidate may be returned, with converged=False.
execution.state_ownership: The trial deep-copies call inputs; the optimizer owns the log, budget and historical valid records. Each call has independent state and never reuses a failed equilibrium.
execution.failure_propagation: Static control errors are rejected first; fixed-size numerical failures are returned with state; budget exhaustion and optimizer stops are separated from forward success.

feedback.state: Parameter vector, fixed N, log, valid best and actual scientific-call count.
feedback.initialization: Initial values and bounds are validated first; the log is empty, best is undetermined and the scientific-call count is zero.
feedback.update_order: Optional LHS; local optimizer trials and numerical differences; fresh terminal validation; freshly validate a valid historical candidate only when necessary.
feedback.continue_when: The optimizer needs a new trial and budget remains after reserving the terminal call.
feedback.stop_when: The optimizer stops, a numerical exception occurs or the budget is exhausted; only an optimizer success whose actual fresh terminal validation passes is marked converged.
feedback.iteration_bound: max_evaluations is the upper bound on all actual scientific calls, default 200 and at least 3.
feedback.nonconvergence: Return the freshly validated partial valid solution and separated state; on complete failure return a None candidate and an N-vector penalty; invalid configurations are not retried.
